traced_paths.audio: UxPlay 1.73.7 (installed ~/.local/bin/uxplay; source /home/maslos/Work/iphone-linux/vendor/UxPlay df67c21, read only). renderers/audio_renderer.c: pipeline 'appsrc ! queue ! avdec_aac ! audioconvert ! audioresample quality=10 ! volume ! level ! <-as> sync=<video_sync>'. With -vsync no, AAC (mirror) buffers get no PTS and the sink has sync=false. lib/raop_buffer.c: with resends active a missing packet holds dequeue until it arrives or the 256-entry buffer overruns (DELAY up to ~255 frames), then releases the backlog at once. audio_renderer_flush() is empty.
traced_paths.video: renderers/video_renderer.c: with -vrtp the pipeline is 'appsrc ! queue ! h264parse ! rtph264pay <Tomacco pipeline>' and the sync flag (static, default false) is only set for UxPlay's own sinks, so -vrtp video is untimestamped whether or not -vsync is given. Tomacco decodes it independently (src/nativeview.cpp, newest-frame-only presentation). Exact A/V lip sync is therefore absent by design: the Annex-B TCP hop drops sender PTS.
traced_paths.input: src/nativeview.cpp sends hover/down/move/up/cancel per mouse event over one control-socket request each, coalescing only the newest queued move/hover. native/runtime.rs worker -> coordination::worker_input (admission) -> runtime/airplay.rs input -> bluetooth.rs Hid::point (BlueZ GATT notification on report 4). Listening = the phone's StartNotify on the pointer report.

defects.root_cause: -vsync no makes UxPlay's mirror audio sink unsynchronised (sync=false, no timestamps): it never drops or skips. Audio that arrives late in a burst (Wi-Fi stall, RTP resend wait in raop_buffer) is played in full afterwards, the sink's ring buffer and upstream queues hold the excess, and the added delay stays until the mirror ends. Sender/sink clock drift accumulates the same way.
defects.evidence: Offline fixture tests/airplay_audio_backlog_integration.py builds UxPlay's own AAC pipeline string (AAC-LC caps 1210, same avdec_aac path as mirror AAC-ELD) and replaces only the device element by a real-time 200 ms ring-buffer model (pulsesink default buffer-time; blocking like a full ring). Legacy plain sink: a 1.2 s stall adds 1190.0 ms and a 2.4 s stall 2390.1 ms of delay until the end of the run (exit 1). The delay equals the stall: it never recovers.
defects.fix: UxPlay gets -as 'queue max-size-buffers=0 max-size-bytes=0 max-size-time=100000000 leaky=downstream ! autoaudiosink' (UxPlay still appends sync=false; default sink unchanged). The queue never blocks upstream and drops its oldest audio beyond 100 ms. If $UXPLAYRC, ~/.uxplayrc or ~/.config/uxplayrc sets 'as'/'-as', Tomacco passes no -as (argv would otherwise override the person's sink) and runtime.state audio_backlog_ms is null; otherwise 100.
defects.fixture_result_after: 1.2 s stall: +330.8 ms; 2.4 s stall: +323.5 ms (ring 200 + queue 100 + about one frame; bound asserted 369.7 ms); 0.86 s / 2.07 s of stale stalled audio dropped. Jitter up to 60 ms: 4.992 of 4.992 s played, latency 63.9 -> 64.9 ms, identical to legacy (no loss, no added base latency). Production string parses with the real autoaudiosink (NULL state only, no device opened): sink sync=false, queue max-size-time 100000000.
defects.not_claimed: No end-to-end or iPhone latency was measured. Steady-state latency is unchanged by design (the queue is empty without a backlog); the fix bounds growth, it does not reduce the sink's own ~200 ms buffer, the phone's encoding delay or the network. Whether this mechanism is the cause of the user's reported delay is unproven until a hardware trace.

defects.root_cause: An up/cancel arriving while the phone was not listening returned early (bluetooth_not_paired / delivered:false) without clearing `held`; hover reported with `self.held`. After the phone listened again (BLE reconnect, re-subscription), every plain mouse hover was sent with the button down, i.e. dragged on the phone. A reconnect between two inputs was invisible because only the boolean listening flag was read.
defects.fix: bluetooth.rs counts StartNotify per characteristic (Notify{on, starts}); Hid::subscriptions(). Airplay forgets held button and pointer position whenever the phone is not listening or its subscription count changed, so the next press moves and settles first. A hover never carries a button and does not move a finger that is down (delivered:false), matching coordination Kind::Pointer 'cannot press anything'.

defects.root_cause: A hover within PACE (8 ms) of the previous report returned delivered:true without sending. The last position of a quick mouse movement was often lost; the desktop hides its own cursor while the phone listens, so the visible phone pointer stayed short of where a click would then land.
defects.fix: Hovers are paced by report()'s existing sleep instead of dropped; the desktop already keeps only the newest pending hover, so no backlog builds.

defects.root_cause: A release at a point the last move did not reach sent move + button-up in one report; the documented iOS behaviour for presses (a button change lands where the pointer was before the report, SETTLE) means the drag can end short. A cancel let go at the cancel's coordinates, i.e. moved the held finger before lifting.
defects.fix: release() first reports the end point with the button held when it differs, then lets go there (one extra 8 ms report, same end state if iOS applies both at once). cancel lets go where the pointer is. Swipes already end on their last step and gain no report.
defects.not_claimed: iOS release-position behaviour is inferred from the measured press behaviour, not measured here.

defects.root_cause: capabilities() always advertised live_touch, 12 keys, text and fill even when BlueZ could not serve the HID device (bluetooth.status unavailable), though every input then fails.
defects.fix: Without a served HID: live_touch/text/fill/exact_scroll false, max_contacts 0, keys [], note naming runtime.state bluetooth.error. With a served HID the capabilities are as before, the note says input needs pairing/listening (runtime.state bluetooth.listening).

observed_not_changed: The 'Control needs Bluetooth' error carries the generic airplay_runtime remedy about ports/firewall (pre-existing; an error-code/remedy change was out of scope).
Each pointer event is one control-socket connection plus a coordination admission transaction; not measured as a defect here, coordination contracts left untouched.

UxPlay's resend wait and empty audio flush remain upstream behaviour; with the fix their backlog is dropped beyond 100 ms instead of kept. A short gap/discontinuity at a stall is expected and audible; nothing is muted.
UxPlay -al (advertised latency) and pulsesink buffer-time are unchanged: no measurement supports changing them.
user_facing_text: No QML/C++/i18n strings changed; the 51 catalogs are untouched (1889 source keys, digest 5d7260fd1b72; tests/python test_i18n passed). Changed English texts are agent-facing JSON (capability note) and docs (CHANGELOG.md, docs/iphone.md).

hardware_qualification_plan.preconditions: Integrated build installed by root; Pixel/iPhone released to this work; the user's own live iPhone runtime is not reused or stopped. No UxPlay startup file with 'as' (it disables the bound by design); for diagnostics an UXPLAYRC containing only 'd' is fine.
checks: Receiver: runtime.state audio_backlog_ms == 100; `ps -o args` of the uxplay child shows the -as queue; uxplay.log shows no GStreamer audio error.

A/V offset: play a flash+click sync video on the iPhone while mirroring; film the desktop screen and record the desktop speaker with one 240 fps camera; measure click-vs-flash at 1, 10 and 30 min. Compare with the pre-change installed build on the same network.

Stall recovery: during playback cause a Wi-Fi stall (walk out of range or briefly block the AP), then measure again within 10 s; pass: the offset returns to within ~0.35 s of the pre-stall value instead of growing by the stall length. Read-only `pactl -f json list sink-inputs` (sink_usec, buffer_usec) before/after.

Swipes (paired, AssistiveTouch on): 20 vertical scrolls in Settings, 20 Home-screen page swipes, 20 fast flicks, 20 slow drags released away from the last move; record the phone screen: each must move content once, with no tap at the start and no short end.

Reconnect: start a drag, turn the phone's Bluetooth off before releasing, release, turn Bluetooth on, wait for bluetooth.listening true, hover across icons: no drag/scroll may happen; then a click must land where the pointer shows. bluetooth.log records the reconnect.
Pointer accuracy: move fast then stop over 10 small targets and click; the phone pointer must sit on the target before the click and the tap must hit it.
Regression: tap, keyboard text, Home (Command-H), volume keys, wheel scrolling and frame-edge swipes as before; a session without Bluetooth shows input_capabilities live_touch false.

final_source_ready_meaning: Source, tests and docs are committed and ready for root integration/packaging. It does not mean the physical AirPlay audio delay or swipe issues are solved: physical_issues_solved stays false until the hardware plan passes on a released device.
preserved: Receiver startup/ownership, mirroring detection, window opening, project chooser, runtime reservations/idempotency/approval contracts, other transports, keyboard, wheel scrolling, live gestures and all i18n catalogs. No push, tag, release, installed binary, global config, device, Bluetooth or network access.
